subject: Post-call: spend trajectory readout, proposed pilot and decision asks
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit@widgetpay.com>, Nina Brooks <nina@widgetpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — spend trajectory, pain points, and proposed pilot

Hi Amit / Nina — thanks again for the 30-minute call earlier. Quick recap to make sure we’re aligned and to capture the asks we agreed on: 

Key pain points you shared
- Token spend spikes during peak checkout flows (monthly burst up to ~3x baseline).
- Latency sensitivity at 95/99p during checkout — target 95p < 150ms, 99p < 300ms.
- Tight budget for POC: you indicated ~USD 15k/month for inference while you validate merchant conversion impact.

Goals for a short pilot
- Validate end-to-end latency and customer-visible latency uplift with caching + batching enabled.
- Demonstrate at least 25–30% token cost reduction on your predicted production mix (orig. estimate in the sheet).
- Produce a 4–6 week operational playbook to move from hosted proof→dedicated pool if results meet SLA and economics.

Redwood observations / hypothesis (from call + logs you shared)
- Checkout traffic has a high prefix reuse rate (sessions with repeated prompts) — opportunity for prefix/KV cache to cut token volume by reusing messages.
- Batchable requests in async reconciliation path (~40% of traffic) can be batched without user-facing latency impact during non-peak minutes.
- Fallback policy needed for peak sudden bursts to avoid tail latency increases.

Recommended pilot configuration (short, measurable)
1) Duration: 3 weeks live + 1 week baseline measurement.
2) Mode: Hosted API with prefix caching and 2-second controlled batching window for reconciliation path.
3) Success metrics: >=25% token reduction vs baseline, 95p latency below 150ms for critical route, no more than 5% error/latency regressions.
4) Cost framing: attached spreadsheet includes three scenarios (conservative, expected, aggressive) for per-10k-token effective cost and projected savings if caching + batching are applied.

Quick numbers (high level) — ballpark per-10k-token cost and pilot ROI
- Hosted baseline (no caching/batching): effective cost ~USD 14–18 per 10k tokens (varies by sequence length; see sheet).
- With caching + batching applied: expected effective cost ~USD 9–12 per 10k tokens (30–35% savings in our expected case).
- If WidgetPay’s pilot traffic matches the call profile, a 30% savings on your projected 300M token/month workload would be ~USD 1.5–2.0k saving per week — pilot payback < 3 months (subject to baseline accuracy).

Attachments: redwood-spend-forecast-20270421.xlsx (detailed scenario sheet), prefix-cache-proposal.pdf (technical approach & ops checklist).

Next steps (proposed)
- WidgetPay: confirm pilot window and which routes to instrument (checkout + async-recon).
- Redwood: provide a scoped pilot SOW and a baseline capture script to run for 7 days pre-change.
- Internal: Marissa/Ben — I’ll need a quick pricing note and a pilot discount structure we can offer within the $15k/mo constraint.

Would you be able to confirm pilot routes and an ideal start week by EOD Friday? Happy to hop on a 15-min sync if helpful.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan_blake@redwood.ai]

From: Amit Shah <amit@widgetpay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nina Brooks <nina@widgetpay.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — spend trajectory, pain points, and proposed pilot

Thanks Jordan — useful recap. A few clarifying Qs before we lock dates: 

1) The per-10k-token numbers — can you break those down by long vs short prompts? Our average checkout prompt is ~120 tokens but some fraud-check flows are ~1.8k tokens.
2) The $15k/month cap is firm for the immediate experiment — we can potentially increase if we see clear conversion uplift but need a conservative pilot offer.
3) SLA ask: if we see tail latency issues during warm-up spikes, what automatic fallbacks would Redwood use and what visibility will we have in Console to triage?

If you can send a compact per-route cost table and an ops-runbook for fallbacks, we’ll review and align. Happy to start baseline capture next week if the ask is lightweight.

—Amit
Amit Shah
Head of Payments Engineering, WidgetPay
[amit@widgetpay.com]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit@widgetpay.com>, Nina Brooks <nina@widgetpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — spend trajectory, pain points, and proposed pilot

Great questions — answers inline and a short per-route table below. I’m attaching a 1-page ops note here (included in the drive link) and will follow with a one-slide pricing summary.

1) Token cost by sequence length (illustrative effective rates)
- Short prompts (~120 tokens avg): baseline hosted effective cost ~USD 8–10 per 10k tokens; with caching/batching ~USD 5–7 per 10k tokens.
- Long prompts (~1.8k tokens avg): baseline hosted effective cost ~USD 28–34 per 10k tokens; with caching savings smaller in absolute terms but still ~20% reduction to ~USD 22–27 per 10k tokens.

2) Pilot discounting / budget framing
- We can structure a capped pilot package: USD 12k for a 4-week scoped pilot (covers hosted usage up to X tokens, plus enablement time). Overage rates apply but we’ll agree limits/alerts first.
- If you prefer performance-anchored discounts (e.g., 30% savings observed → partial credit), we can bake that into the SOW.

3) Failover & Console visibility
- Automatic fallback policy: when we detect tail latency > configured threshold for the route, requests are routed to a lighter-weight model variant (lower compute) and we emit a real-time alert.
- Console: you’ll get a per-route latency histogram, token burn dashboard, and trace links for any anomalous spike. We’ll add a dashboard tile for the pilot to surface 95/99p and cache hit rate.

Per-route example (projected monthly mix)
- checkout (interactive): 55% of inference tokens, avg prompt 120 tokens — pilot target: 30% reduction in token volume via cache reuse and micro-batching of non-critical sub-requests.
- fraud-check (async): 25% of tokens, avg prompt 1.8k — batching in hourly windows reduces overhead for this flow (non-customer-facing).
- reconciliation (batch): 20% — high potential for aggressive batching (>3x amortization of per-request overhead).

Pilot next steps
- We’ll prepare a 1-page SOW and the baseline capture script (simple proxy to log token counts + latencies) by tomorrow EOD.
- Amit: if you can confirm routes (checkout, fraud-check, reconciliation) and a preferred pilot start date window (week of Apr 26 or May 3), I’ll lock the SOW and send the pilot quote.

I’ll also loop Marissa to confirm the commercial terms I proposed above and Ben for the econ model.

Best,
Jordan

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 17:46:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap — spend trajectory, pilot ask (internal)

Marissa / Ben — forwarding the thread so we can align on the commercial and econ side. Key points for internal decisioning: 

- Customer cap: they want to keep near USD 15k/mo for the experiment. I proposed a capped pilot at USD 12k for 4 weeks to stay within their ceiling. Need your signoff or suggestions on adjustments.
- Metrics to guarantee/discount against: 30% token reduction and target 95p latency < 150ms for checkout. If achieved, we can offer a conversion credit or rollout discount.
- Attachments: spend model + ops notes in the Drive link. Ben — can you run a quick sensitivity that shows payback period at 20/25/30% savings (assume current token burn baseline in the sheet)?
- Marissa — we may want to include a small professional services line (up to 8 hours) to instrument baseline capture and the Console dashboard; propose we waive that for the pilot to reduce friction.

Suggested reply: confirm pilot routes and offer the USD 12k/4-week capped pilot with an explicit overage alert threshold at 10% — ask Chris Legal to sign a light SOW. If that sound OK, I’ll send the pilot quote to Amit and Nina.

Thanks — Jordan
